advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confine the REBAR_TRACKER_DIR override to a single-threaded context (or pass the tracker dir explicitly to the reader) so the process-global env mutation cannot leak to concurrent config readers.
evidence: prior = os.environ.get("REBAR_TRACKER_DIR")  # read-via: multi-store-tracker-relocation
os.environ["REBAR_TRACKER_DIR"] = tracker_path  # read-via: multi-store-tracker-relocation
config.py tracker_dir_override(): return os.environ.get("REBAR_TRACKER_DIR") or None (read live, no caching, no lock)
advisory.finding: _read_ticket_state_via_env_override mutates the process-global os.environ (sets REBAR_TRACKER_DIR, restores in finally). This is shared global mutable state: if build_labels ever runs on a background thread or concurrently with any other code reading REBAR_TRACKER_DIR / config (which reads the env live per tracker_dir_override), the override leaks across the boundary and the other reader targets the wrong store.
scenarios: build_labels invoked from a threaded harness or test-parallel runner while another thread resolves the tracker dir
a signal handler or atexit hook reading config mid-override

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Use f.get("norm_id") with a skip/guard (or validate norm_id presence in _findings_for_row) so a finding missing norm_id cannot KeyError-crash build_labels.
evidence: _findings_for_row docstring: 'An unmatched or unreadable body degrades to an empty finding list rather than raising -- this driver's job is to always produce a valid labels file'
classify_finding_survival: k1_ids = {f["norm_id"] for f in review_k1} and f["norm_id"] in the comprehension (hard key access)
_criterion_sets: sets.setdefault(criterion, set()).add(f["norm_id"])
per_question_agreement: k_by_id = {f["norm_id"]: f for f in review_k}
sidecar._slim persists norm_id for well-formed rows (sidecar.py:665), but nothing validates the re-read REVIEW_RESULT body findings carry it before hard-indexing
advisory.finding: _findings_for_row promises to 'always produce a valid labels file' and degrades unreadable bodies to [], but the pure functions it feeds (classify_finding_survival, _criterion_sets, per_question_agreement) access f["norm_id"] as a hard key. A finding lacking norm_id (legacy/malformed sidecar row, or a hand-authored finding) raises KeyError and crashes build_labels — defeating the stated best-effort degradation.
scenarios: a differing-material pair whose REVIEW_RESULT body carries a finding dict without a norm_id key

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a build_labels test with a ticket carrying two review_result events (identical material_fingerprint, differing verdict) asserting pair_with_previous={pair_kind: 'identical_material', noise_flip: True}, and one with differing material asserting the finding_survival/criterion_churn/question_agreement pair labels.
evidence: build_labels: `for i, row in enumerate(ticket_rows): ... if i > 0: out_row["pair_with_previous"] = _label_pair(ticket_rows[i - 1], row, event_index, store_roots)` (labels.py:510-516)

Both E2E tests write a single review_result per ticket: test_build_labels_writes_a_hash_keyed_file_and_load_labels_round_trips and test_build_labels_ticket_labels_reflect_escaped_defect_via_stub each call tracker.review_result exactly once (test_plan_replay_labels.py:341,386)
search_files for `pair_with_previous` in tests: (no matches); search for `identical_material` in tests: only the pure-function test at line 107, none through build_labels

Module docstring names the pair path as its purpose: 'two reviews of byte-identical material ... that land different verdicts (:func:`noise_flip`) are pure reviewer variance ... that variance rate is the floor' (labels.py docstring)
advisory.finding: The pair-labeling path in build_labels (the module's headline reviewer-noise/churn feature) has no end-to-end test: every build_labels test creates exactly one review per ticket, so the `if i > 0` branch that computes pair_with_previous via _label_pair (noise_flip, identical_material vs differing_material, classify_finding_survival, per_criterion_churn, per_question_agreement, _findings_for_row, _build_event_index) never executes.
scenarios: A ticket with two review_result events of identical material_fingerprint but verdict PASS then BLOCK should yield pair_with_previous={pair_kind: identical_material, noise_flip: True}; nothing constructs this, so a regression in _label_pair, the ordering sort, or event_index wiring would ship green.

A ticket with two reviews of differing material should populate finding_survival/criterion_churn/question_agreement from re-read REVIEW_RESULT bodies via _findings_for_row+_build_event_index; that integration is never driven.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test exercising _read_ticket_state_via_env_override that asserts REBAR_TRACKER_DIR is restored to its prior value (both prior-set and prior-unset cases) after the call.
evidence: _read_ticket_state_via_env_override sets and restores the env var: `prior = os.environ.get("REBAR_TRACKER_DIR")` ... `finally: if prior is None: os.environ.pop(...) else: os.environ["REBAR_TRACKER_DIR"] = prior` (labels.py:289-297)
Every build_labels test passes read_ticket_state=_stub_ticket_state(...), bypassing the real reader (test_plan_replay_labels.py:358,403)
search_files for `_read_ticket_state_via_env_override` in tests: (no matches)
advisory.finding: _read_ticket_state_via_env_override — the real multi-store reader with the REBAR_TRACKER_DIR set/restore finally-block — is stubbed out in every test (read_ticket_state=_stub_ticket_state(...)), so neither the env-override behavior nor the prior-None-vs-prior-set restore branches are exercised.
scenarios: If the restore branch (prior set vs unset) regressed, leaking REBAR_TRACKER_DIR into the caller's environment, no test would notice.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend TrackerBuilder (or add a focused test) to write STATUS/COMMENT/COMPLETION_VERDICT events and assert _ticket_status_events returns them oldest-first and that reopen_count/force_close reflect real reconstructed events.
evidence: _ticket_status_events filters `b.kind in _STATUS_KINDS` = {STATUS, COMMENT, COMPLETION_VERDICT} and reconstructs events from git blobs (labels.py:262-278)
TrackerBuilder only exposes create() (CREATE) and review_result() (REVIEW_RESULT); no method writes STATUS/COMMENT/COMPLETION_VERDICT events (test_plan_replay_labels.py:58-72)
_ticket_labels_for calls _ticket_status_events unstubbed even when read_ticket_state is a stub (labels.py:318), so E2E runs return [] for events
advisory.finding: _ticket_status_events reading real STATUS/COMMENT/COMPLETION_VERDICT git blobs is never driven end-to-end: the E2E trackers contain only CREATE and REVIEW_RESULT events, so reopen_count/force_close/completion_verifier_fail_count over real reconstructed events are only ever tested via synthetic dicts, never through the git-object-walk in _ticket_status_events.
scenarios: A regression in the _STATUS_KINDS filter, the ts sort, or the json body parsing in _ticket_status_events would not be caught, since no test feeds it a tracker containing those event kinds.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert render_report emits the correct '## Finding-level (pair) labels' counts for labeled_rows containing pair_with_previous entries.
evidence: render_report: `if pair_counts: for kind in sorted(pair_counts): lines.append(f"- {kind}: {pair_counts[kind]}")` (labels.py:375-377)
The only report assertion checks 'Plan-review outcome labels' and 'escaped_defect: 1' (test_plan_replay_labels.py:365,414); neither drives a pair count because no test creates consecutive reviews
advisory.finding: render_report's pair-counts branch is untested: no test produces a labeled row with pair_with_previous, so the `if pair_counts:` branch (lines 375-377) that emits '## Finding-level (pair) labels' entries never runs; only the empty-pair fallback and the ticket-level path are covered.
scenarios: A regression in the pair_counts aggregation or its report rendering would not be detected.
